newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending growth slowed in Q4 - BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending growth slowed in Q4 - BBA.

text.p: Growth in lending by major British banks slowed in the fourth quarter of last year, the British Bankers Association (BBA) said on Thursday.
Over the three months to the end of December, total lending increased by 6,085 million stg, compared to a revised figure of 7,031 million stg for the previous quarter.
Within that total, lending to individuals rose by around 3.05 billion pounds, marginally up on the third quarter.
"Overall, the lending figures are down on the previous quarter, though in part this reflects a rundown of repo lending and investment," said BBA director-general Tim Sweeney.
Lending through reverse repos fell by nearly 600 million pounds over the quarter.

Individuals, industrial and commercial companies accounted for the bulk of the new lending, the BBA said. Overall lending to financial companies was modest, following buoyant growth over the previous six months.
"The major banks' lending throughout the year was driven by personal demand, both for mortgages and consumer credit which grew by five and 13 percent respectively," Sweeney said.
He said lending to the financial sector was nine percent stronger over the year as a whole although it fluctuated from quarter to quarter.
Borrowing by industry and commerce rose by five percent over the year.
